title: My first game is playable, and releasing it on Steam is my next dream. I’d love your honest feedback.
author: abner-ruza
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Yesterday I released another game I’d been working on, and it was really well received. That gave me the confidence to share **CytoSquad** with you too.

CytoSquad is my first game, and making it has been a dream come true. There’s something surreal about seeing an idea turn into something people can actually play.

It’s an action survival roguelite set inside the human body. You control an immune cell fighting viruses, bacteria, and bosses, either solo or with up to 4 players in online co-op. I’m building it in Godot with AI assistance.

**The playable beta is available now for Windows** in itch io

I really want to bring it to Steam someday, but honestly, I’m afraid it’ll flop. I’m proud of how far I’ve come, but I’d love some outside perspective on what’s working and what still needs improvement.

* Does the concept catch your interest?
* If you try it, what feels fun, confusing, or frustrating?
* What would you want improved before a Steam release?

Honest criticism is welcome. Making my first game was a dream; now I want to learn how to make it better.

Thanks for taking a look!

comments.body: Thank you! 😊 It took me about 6 months. It’s my first game, so there was a lot of learning along the way. Really happy you liked it!

replies.author: xevlar
replies.body: Are you blind by any chance?

replies.author: abner-ruza
replies.body:
Honestly, the main difference is that Plague Inc. is a strategy game where you spread a disease. In CytoSquad, you’re on the other side: you control an immune cell directly, fight waves of enemies, and build up your abilities as you go.

It’s closer to Vampire Survivors, but inside the human body, and you can play with up to 3 friends. I wanted each organ to feel like its own battlefield, with different enemies and hazards.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
That's looking really good, IMHO!

It feels pretty polished overall. The UI is probably the one thing that still feels a little messy, and honestly, that's one of the few things that would make me suspect it was AI-generated.

I'm also not the biggest fan of the music, personally, but that's just a matter of taste.

Other than that, keep up the good work! Put together a solid trailer to showcase it, get it on Steam (make sure to also include some achievements), and I could definitely see this making some sales in an already oversaturated market for these kinds of games.

Good luck!

replies.author: abner-ruza
replies.body:
Thank you so much for the thoughtful feedback! I really appreciate you pointing out the UI and music. I’ll take another look at the UI and see how I can make it cleaner.

A good trailer, Steam release, and achievements are all things I’d love to work toward. Hearing that you think the game could find an audience is really encouraging, especially since this is my first game.

Thanks again for taking the time to check it out!

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
My pleasure! 

Here are a few more specific tips that might help you polish the game before releasing it on Steam:

**1. Steam Achievements**

Adding achievements through Steam is relatively straightforward, especially with AI to help you. Ask an LLM to guide you through the setup process, and you should be able to get everything up and running in no time.

**2. Your Trailer**

Make the most of AI when creating your trailer. Start by brainstorming ideas with an LLM, exploring different concepts, pacing, and ways to showcase the game's strongest features. Then use those ideas to help create the trailer with AI.

Just remember to add that essential human touch afterwards: polish the result, review the quality, and make sure everything feels cohesive.

**3. Simplify Your HUD**

One thing that stands out to me is that there's quite a lot of text in your HUD.

Remember, players are already familiar with common gaming conventions. If they see a green bar, most will immediately assume it's a health bar. You don't necessarily need to spell it out. The bar and a number should be more than enough. The same principle applies to experience points.

The goal is to communicate information clearly without overwhelming the player with unnecessary text.

**4. Make Your Power-Up Icons Do the Talking**

I'd apply the same principle to the power-ups in the bottom-right corner.

There's nothing wrong with giving them fun names, such as "Diagonal Poopy Inflator Beam", but those names don't necessarily need to be displayed permanently on the HUD.

Instead, focus on making each icon instantly recognisable. When a player pauses the game or selects a power-up, that's the perfect opportunity to display its full name and explain what it does.

Keep the HUD clean and let the icons speak for themselves.

**5. Clean Up the Information in the Top-Left Corner**

I'd also consider reducing the amount of written information in the top-left corner.

For example, "Insane" could be represented by a difficulty icon, with consistent, related icons for the other difficulty levels.

I'd argue that the wave number is useful information to display, but "Active Viruses" doesn't necessarily need a written label. Showing the number as 152/200 already communicates the information effectively.

Think about which details players genuinely need to see at a glance and which ones can be communicated more simply.

**6. Improve the Overall HUD Layout**

Try to create more visual balance across the HUD. Look for elements that could be aligned along an invisible grid or ruler.

Even small adjustments to spacing, alignment, and consistency can make the entire interface feel much more polished and professional.

**7. Reconsider the Music**

Lastly, a quick note on the music. This is very subjective, so take it with a pinch of salt, but personally, I don't feel that the current music quite fits the scenes.

It might be worth experimenting with a few alternatives to see whether you can find something that better complements the gameplay, atmosphere, and overall tone of the game.

Of course, this is just my personal opinion!

Good luck with getting the game onto Steam!

replies.author: abner-ruza
replies.body:
Wow, thank you so much for taking the time to write all of this! It’s really nice to get thoughtful, constructive feedback like yours.

I’ve noted everything down, and I’m going to rethink the UI and HUD. You’re right that there’s text everywhere 😅 I’ll look at how I can make things clearer with less text on screen.

Thanks again, this really helps!

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
Good stuff: I'm glad you see some value in it, so I've not typed it for nothing. :-)  
Keep up the good work.
